findings.title: `call(...)?` (EX_TRY) is invisible to the escape set, so a local published through a call goes into a block arena: generated C has a heap-use-after-free
findings.why: The escape set E (c->escapees) is the only input to isEscapeeName(), which check_expr.c:3686 (method receiver) and callHomeDepth (check_top.c:1616-1622) use to pick the arena handed to a callee. ST_EXPR classifies only EX_CALL/EX_METHOD/EX_ASSOC; a call written with the error/option propagation operator `?` is an EX_TRY node wrapping the call, so it falls into `default: return false` and nothing is marked. A local container that is filled through such a call is therefore not an escapee, its receiver reports placeDepth = 1 instead of -1, and the callee allocates into the current *block* arena of the caller's frame instead of the home arena. Everything the callee stored into that container is released when the block/frame ends. `EX_EXT` (`ext f(x)`) has the same gap for the same reason.
findings.trigger: A function that (a) declares a local container, (b) fills it with an option-returning method/function whose only publication in the body is written `call(...)?`, and (c) publishes the container into a caller's `mut ref` out-parameter, also with `?`. This is the ordinary stdlib style (`out.put(x)?`).
findings.repro: cp /tmp/rev/findings/tryb3.extc /tmp/tryb3.extc; cd /home/alphayang/extC_Compiler; ./build/extc -w /tmp/tryb3.extc -o /tmp/tryb3.c   # accepted, exit 0; gcc -fwrapv -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -o /tmp/tryb3 /tmp/tryb3.c && /tmp/tryb3  ->  'ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free ... in main /tmp/tryb3.extc:40'. Control: tests/arena-promoted/B3_exprstmt_method.extc is the same program without `?`; it is clean ('head = 7'). EXTC_DUMP_EFFECTS=1 shows `[escapes] fill { }` for the `?` version against `[escapes] fill { l out }` for the control. Expected: E contains `l`, or the call site rejects the publication.

findings.title: `fresh` local set is built once from declarations and never invalidated by retargeting: the callee's effect summary comes out empty and the call-site lifetime rule is skipped
findings.why: The `fresh` exemption assumes a name in `fresh` still holds the object its *declaration* allocated. collectFreshLocals (check_top.c:1889-1908) adds the name from the initializer only and nothing ever removes it; classifyStoredValue then answers 'the source is fresh, so no lifetime constraint' for a store of that name into a `mut ref` container parameter even after the name was retargeted to a value derived from a parameter. The summary stays all-zero with effComplete = true, so in checkCallRefArgs (1259-1266) both addrMaybe and contMaybe are false and every check of every argument of that callee is skipped. With the bare `n = target` form the retarget store itself is classified as a store into the home arena (classifyStoredValue with intoHome = true sets homeAddrMask), which happens to mask the hole; routing the value through any call (`n = id(target)`, a complete callee) removes that accident.
findings.trigger: A callee with `mut ref container` out-parameter and a `ref`-like source parameter, whose body does: `var n: T = new ...` (so n enters `fresh`), then `n = <expression derived from the source parameter that is not a bare parameter identifier>` (a call is the simplest), then `out.field = n`.

READ of size 4 ... in main /tmp/fresh2.extc:17'. Control (/tmp/rev/findings/fresh1.extc) writes `n = target` directly and is correctly rejected with 'argument 2 of `stash` points into a deeper scope (depth 2) than the arena this call may store it in (depth 1)'.

findings.title: Effect-summary masks are 32 bits but a function may have more than 32 parameters: `1u << j` is UB and every argument at index >= 32 is never checked
findings.why: params.len is unbounded (a 40-parameter function compiles cleanly), but addrMask/contMask/homeAddrMask/homeContMask are `unsigned` and are indexed by the parameter position j = paramIndex(...). For j >= 32 `1u << j` is undefined behaviour; on x86-64 it wraps (1u << 32 == 1u, 1u << 33 == 2u), so the flow is recorded against parameter 1 instead of parameter 33. In addition the loops that consume the masks stop at `j < 32` (check_top.c:1223 for the extern path and check_top.c:1403 for the by-value/content-flow path), so arguments from the 33rd on are never examined at all: no mask bit can ever describe them. Observed on a 33-parameter callee: the store of parameter 33 lands on bit 0 (EXTC_DBG_REFARGS prints cont=0x1) and is then checked against argument 1, an i32, which is skipped; the real argument is never reported.
findings.trigger: A callee with 33 or more parameters where a reference-carrying by-value argument at index >= 32 (a struct holding a `ref`, a view, ...) is stored into a `mut ref` container parameter, or where the address of a `mut ref` argument at index >= 32 is stored.
findings.repro: cp /tmp/rev/findings/wide2.extc /tmp/wide2.extc; cd /home/alphayang/extC_Compiler; ./build/extc -w /tmp/wide2.extc -o /tmp/wide2.c   # accepted, exit 0 (31 i32 params, then `s: mut ref slot`, then `v: cell`); gcc -fwrapv -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -o /tmp/wide2 /tmp/wide2.c && /tmp/wide2 -> 'ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-use-after-scope ... in main /tmp/wide2.extc:13'. Control /tmp/rev/findings/small2.extc is the same function with 4 parameters and is rejected: 'argument 2 of `stash` carries a reference into a deeper scope (depth 2) than the place the callee may store it (depth 1)'. Related, smaller: wide.extc (34 params, ref flow) is rejected only because the address-flow loop iterates over all params and uses the mask merely as a gate.

findings.title: The level solver's step budget only prints a message: it never stops the walk, and the message claims it was stopped
findings.why: `ls->loud` guards the *message* only. There is no early return after ctxError, and `loud`/`steps` are read nowhere else (only 3091-3098 and the initialisation at 3467), so once the budget is exceeded the walk keeps recursing with the same exponential path structure the budget was added for (the cycle cut at 3084-3090 is path-local, so a diamond in the value graph still yields 2^n visits). The compiler prints an internal-error message and then keeps running, potentially for hours: the diagnostic says 'was stopped', which is false, and a caller who sees it has no way to know that the process is still burning CPU. The file's own comment (3019-3027) justifies the budget as 'a compiler that hangs has no message and no position ... is strictly worse', but the code implements only the message, not the stop.
findings.trigger: Any input whose level walk exceeds 4,000,000 visited (value,target) pairs. I could not build one (tried nested `??` chains up to depth 32: EXTC_DBG_LV shows the walk stops at the first binding; a 32-parameter function does not reach the walk either), so the trigger is conditional - but that the guard does not stop anything is a code fact, not a guess.
findings.repro: Read src/check_top.c:3082-3106 and grep for `loud`/`steps`: `grep -rn 'loud\|ls->steps' src/` returns only 3091-3098 and 3467. No program-driven reproduction; attempting one with a 20-deep nested `??` (`/tmp/rev/findings/coal.extc`) compiled in 4 ms because the walk never descends there.

findings.title: Checker.escapeesFor is written but never read: the documented cross-call memo does not exist and the key is a truncated pointer
findings.code_quote:
computeEscapes(c, f);
    c->escapeesFor = (int)(size_t)f;   /* marks "already computed", keyed by address */
findings.why: grep over the whole tree finds only this write and the declaration in check_internal.h:432 ('function the set was computed for, -1 when not yet'). Nothing ever compares escapeesFor with a FuncDef, so the guard the comment and the declaration describe is absent: collectEffects recomputes computeEscapes for the same body every time it is called for it (checkFunc at 4219, the per-instance loop at 5831/5848, and the closing pass), and the field is dead state that misleads a reader into believing E is cached. If such a guard were added with this key, `(int)(size_t)f` would also be a lossy key: two FuncDefs 2^32 bytes apart collide and the second function would silently inherit the first one's set.
findings.trigger: No user-visible failure; concrete cost is the repeated escape fixpoint over every body (32/64 rounds each) plus a dead, misleading field.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'escapeesFor' src/  -> only src/check_internal.h:432 (declaration) and src/check_top.c:2768 (write).

findings.title: Level pass cost is quadratic in the number of store records of one function
findings.why: For every store record of the function, step two rescans the whole record slice to find the alternative assignments of the same destination (O(S^2) per round, and the slice is rescanned in both fixed-point rounds at 3487 and 3518). On top of that every binding lookup goes through symLevel/setSymLevel (3327-3356), which are linear scans over the binding table, called once per identifier visited by levelOfValue2 (3210-3218, 3152-3172), and the EX_STRUCTLIT case of levelOfValue2 scans the module-wide c->allSyms vector for every struct literal visited (3289-3292). Measured on one function containing S store records (`var vI: ?ref i32 = null` followed by `vI = p`): 0.08 s for S=1000, 0.28 s for S=2000, 1.03 s for S=4000 (approximately 3.7x per doubling = quadratic with a large constant), RSS 9.8 / 14.8 / 22.4 MB. A generated function with ~16k assignments extrapolates to ~16 s of compile time in a single function.
findings.trigger: One function with several thousand assignments to pointer-carrying bindings (generated code, large tables, machine-written sources).
findings.repro: Files /tmp/rev/findings/big1000.extc, big2000.extc, big4000.extc (generator: `var vI: ?ref i32 = null` xN then `vI = p` xN then `return v0`); run `/usr/bin/time -f '%es %MkB' ./build/extc -w bigN.extc -o /dev/null` for N = 1000, 2000, 4000 and observe 0.08/0.28/1.03 s.

coverage_notes: Read all of src/check_top.c:1721-3440 in 500-700 line chunks (plus the callers needed to judge it: check_stmt.c ST_ASSIGN/ST_VAR depth bookkeeping, check_expr.c method-receiver and call-through-fn paths, check_escape.c exprRefDepth/placeRootDepth, check_top.c checkCallRefArgs/computeEffectsTransitive/levelPass/checkFunc, check_internal.h Sym layout). Verified as correct: collectLoopSites/loopIdOf bounds and loop-id threading (i+2 < sites->len is exact for 3-int records; the report only prints facts); reportMemory; fieldDepthEntry's 4-entry cap matches Sym.fields[4] and the strong-update/weak-update split in noteFieldDepthWrite (addressed -> max, complete table -> overwrite, incomplete -> no drop) with refreshRootDepth being monotone in refDepth; noteWholeValueDepthWrite copying src->nfields <= 4 slots is in bounds and its missing isRefRoot guard is unreachable because ref-typed assignment targets return earlier in check_stmt.c:616-769; markNamesInExpr and collectEffectsExpr cover every ExprKind that holds a sub-expression (checked against ast.h:119-170), including EX_DYN payload, EX_SLICE bounds, EX_TRY, EX_EXT and the aggregate shapes; paramIndex is NULL-safe for the callers in this range; levelOfValue's path push/pop is balanced and its (val,target) cut plus hops>32 bound recursion; valueLevel/solvedValDepth/depthComesFromAlloc2 are all live (called from check_top.c:4889/6212); symLevel/setSymLevel only ever lower a level, which is the safe direction. Not reported: the aggregate/pointee-blind EX_TRY form of the ST_EXPR escape gap is part of finding 1; attempts to turn the EX_EXT gap, the 32-round escape fixpoint cap (computeEscapesMode, line 2146) and the >32-parameter full-parameter loops of checkCallRefArgs into separate dangling-pointer reproductions did not succeed (B2/B3-style promotion compensates), so they are folded into the findings above rather than listed on their own.
